scenario.name: LockBit Ransomware Behavioral Analysis: VSS Wipe & Fast Encryption
scenario.shortSubtitle: Malware & Log Analysis · Mutex Creation, WMI Shadow Copy Deletion & I/O Spike
scenario.overview: Imagine a high-speed heist crew that rushes into a records building with two clear orders: first, smash every automatic time-capsule backup cabinet and unplug the emergency repair switch so nobody can rewind the clock; second, unleash a fleet of parallel hardware-powered padlocking presses that lock alternating slices of every filing cabinet across the building in seconds before dropping an extortion card in every room. In this scenario (T1486 / T1490, LockBit Ransomware Behavioral Analysis: VSS Wipe & Fast Encryption), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: deleting All Windows Volume Shadow Copies, then multi-Threaded Intermittent File Encryption. Steps #1–#2 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Deleting All Windows Volume Shadow Copies, then Multi-Threaded Intermittent File Encryption, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: INHIBIT SYSTEM RECOVERY VIA VSS DELETION
stages.subtitle: Terminating SQL/Backup services and wiping Volume Shadow Copies
stages.description: Before touching a single office drawer, the crew sprints straight to the basement recovery room, shreds every automatic historical backup copy silently, and rips out the emergency boot-repair lever so staff cannot restore yesterday's files. Before encrypting a single document, the LockBit 3.0 payload (C:\Windows\Temp\lb3_payload.exe -pass a8f9102b, PID 5540, running with High/Administrator integrity under CORP\admin_srv after registering mutex Global\39481-LB3 and stopping backup services via ControlService) calls CreateProcessW to spawn C:\Windows\System32\vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet (PID 5812, where "delete shadows /all" instructs the Windows Volume Shadow Copy Service to permanently erase every local backup snapshot on the drive so the victim cannot restore clean files for free, and "/quiet" suppresses confirmation prompts). Immediately after, it runs bcdedit /set {default} recoveryenabled No to disable Windows Automatic Repair boot recovery. When vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet (PID 5812, PPID 5540) executes, it invokes IVssBackupComponents::DeleteSnapshots over COM to the Volume Shadow Copy service (vssvc.exe) to drop all copy-on-write shadow storage diff areas on the NTFS volume (because this pre-encryption step happens before file encryption starts, an EDR rule that kills parent PID 5540 the instant Sysmon Event ID 1 logs vssadmin delete shadows stops the ransomware before data loss occurs). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ DELETE SHADOWS / ⇠#1 ACK PID 5812) from Node ① (#1 Breached Admin RDP Jump-Host) to Node ② (#2 Datacenter Core Switch), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 EDR Canary Guard & SOC SIEM).

keySpecs.value: Pre-encryption stage — Kill parent PID 5540 immediately

stages.title: MULTI-THREADED INTERMITTENT FILE ENCRYPTION
stages.subtitle: I/O Completion Ports encrypt file headers and drop ransom notes
stages.description: With recovery doors welded shut, the crew launches parallel processor-accelerated locking gears that stamp only the opening chunks of huge files to corrupt entire servers in moments, tagging every sealed drawer and sliding a ransom note under every door. With local recovery paths eliminated, lb3_payload.exe (PID 5540) uses Windows I/O Completion Ports (an asynchronous multi-threaded disk subsystem that saturates all CPU cores at once) and Intermittent Encryption, encrypting only the first 64 KB of each file on D:\Shares\Finance\* (such as renaming Q4_Budget.xlsx to Q4_Budget.xlsx.lockbit via MoveFileExW) using hardware-accelerated AES-256-NI + RSA-2048 session key wrapping (destroying each file’s 64 KB header so thousands of files are locked in seconds before defenders can react), and writes the 4.1 KB ransom note D:\Shares\Finance\Restore-My-Files.txt in every directory. Full-file encryption on multi-gigabyte databases takes minutes and generates sustained disk I/O spikes that behavioral anti-ransomware minifilters easily spot. Encrypting only the first 64 KB header via MoveFileExW(*.lockbit) and dropping the 4.1 KB Restore-My-Files.txt note ruins file structures at a fraction of the I/O cost (triggering Sysmon Event ID 11 FileCreate alerts and EDR canary file tripwires that isolate the host). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ RANSOM NOTE / ⇠#2 ACK 4.1 KB) from Node ② (#2 Datacenter Core Switch) to Node ③ (#3 Target File Server (FILE-SRV-01)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 EDR Canary Guard & SOC SIEM).

keySpecs.value: Intermittent (First 64 KB per file + RSA footer)

detectionRule.title: Volume Shadow Copy Deletion via Vssadmin / WMIC
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Shadow Copies Deletion Using Operating Systems Utilities
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_vssadmin:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection_vssadmin
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Configure automated EDR prevention policies to suspend/kill the parent process of any unauthorized shadow copy deletion and maintain immutable offline backups.

detectionRule.title: Known Ransomware Note Filename Creation (Sysmon EID 11)
detectionRule.ruleCode:
title: Ransomware Note File Creation
logsource:
  product: windows
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\Restore-My-Files.txt'
      - '\README-LOCKBIT.txt'
      - '\HOW_TO_DECRYPT.txt'
  condition: selection
level: critical
detectionRule.mitigation: Configure Windows File Server Resource Manager (FSRM) file screens to block known ransomware extensions/notes and automatically revoke SMB sessions.
